name_en: Kaki no dotenabe — oyster hot pot with a miso levee around the rim
summary_ja: 土鍋のふちに赤白の味噌を土手のように塗り、崩しながら味を調える広島湾の牡蠣鍋。潮の流れと川の栄養が交わる湾で育つ身の大きな牡蠣を、冬の味覚として一般家庭でも飲食店でも楽しんでいる。
summary_en: Red and white miso are spread like an embankment around the rim of a clay pot, to be crumbled in bit by bit as the broth simmers with plump Hiroshima Bay oysters. Calm currents and river nutrients flowing into the bay are said to give the oysters their size and depth of flavor.
source_title: かきの土手鍋 広島県

name_en: Bishu nabe — sake-simmered chicken and pork hot pot of the brewers' town
summary_ja: 鶏肉や砂ずり、豚肉を塩こしょうと日本酒だけで仕立てた鍋。銘醸地・西条の杜氏が酒造りの合間に食べたまかない料理が始まりで、利き酒の邪魔をしない薄味が特徴と伝わる。
summary_en: Chicken, gizzard, and pork are simmered with nothing more than salt, pepper, and sake in this hot pot from Saijo, one of Japan's noted brewing towns. It is said to have begun as a simple meal cooked by sake brewers between batches, seasoned lightly so as not to dull their palate for tasting.
